Action Plan:
1. Suspected viral upper respiratory tract infection:
   • Advise patient to obtain a digital thermometer and monitor temperature twice daily.  
   • Continue symptomatic relief with Lemsip (contains paracetamol); avoid all other paracetamol-containing products.  
   • Encourage adequate fluids and rest; cough syrup only if nocturnal cough prevents sleep.  
   • Safety-net advice: if temperature ≥ 37.5 – 38 °C persists or spikes, cough worsens, purulent or bloody sputum develops, shortness of breath or chest pain occurs, or nasal bleeding starts, patient to seek re-assessment promptly—possible need for antibiotics.
2. Diabetes management:
   • Reinforce importance of routine blood glucose and HbA1c monitoring as arranged with primary care.  
   • Patient currently lacks home glucose meter; advised to obtain or arrange regular checks with GP/diabetes nurse.
3. Hypertension follow-up:
   • Encourage scheduling of overdue blood-pressure review with GP; confirm current lisinopril dose and control.
4. Medication review / safety:
   • Record current regular medications (metformin, lisinopril) and OTC Lemsip (2–3 sachets/day).  
   • Educate on maximum paracetamol daily dose and avoidance of duplication.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 45-year-old woman (DOB 20 Feb 1958) presents with 5-day history of dry cough (every 20–30 min) and continuous rhinorrhoea with green discharge.  
• Feels intermittently hot with chills; no temperature recorded.  
• No chest pain, dyspnoea, pleuritic pain, haemoptysis.  
• Myalgia present; earlier brief diarrhoea now resolved.  
• No sore ears, sore throat, rash, headache, or visual change.  
Past Medical History: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension. No chronic lung disease.  
Medications:  
  – Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  – Lisinopril 200 mg (dose as stated; frequency not documented)  
  – Lemsip sachets (2–3 per day, dose/route/frequency varies)  
Allergies: No known drug allergies; mild seasonal hay fever.  
Social: Lives with partner and dog; office manager. Occasional alcohol (“the odd sherry”). Smoking status not stated.

Objective:
• Telehealth consult – no in-person examination. No vitals recorded.  
• No investigations performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute cough and rhinorrhoea
   - Assessment: Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection (possible early viral chest infection).
   - Differential: Early bacterial lower respiratory tract infection, allergic rhinitis.
   - Investigations planned: Home temperature monitoring; none immediate.
   - Treatment planned: Symptomatic care (Lemsip, hydration, rest); nocturnal cough syrup only if sleep-disturbing.
   - Safety-netting as above; consider antibiotics if bacterial signs develop.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
   - Assessment: Stable by recent bloods (3 weeks ago), but no home glucose monitoring.
   - Investigations planned: Routine HbA1c and glucose per GP schedule.
   - Treatment planned: Continue metformin; obtain glucose meter or arrange in-clinic monitoring.
   - Relevant referrals: Diabetes nurse/GP for routine review.

3. Hypertension
   - Assessment: Control status unknown (patient unsure of last BP reading).
   - Investigations planned: Blood-pressure check at GP office.
   - Treatment planned: Continue lisinopril; confirm correct dose with GP.
   - Relevant referrals: GP for BP review.

4. Medication safety / paracetamol intake
   - Assessment: Risk of paracetamol overdose if additional products used.
   - Treatment planned: Limit paracetamol to contained dose within 2–3 daily Lemsip sachets; avoid other paracetamol products.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Vital signs (temperature, BP, HR, RR, SpO₂), smoking status clarification, exact metformin and lisinopril doses/frequencies, allergy specifics (NKDA confirmed verbally only).  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor inaudible words but did not affect clinical data extraction.
